serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Cursor is an AI-powered software development platform that helps developers and organizations understand, generate, review, and maintain software. The offering includes the Cursor editor, AI-assisted development workflows, and related cloud services. Anysphere, Inc. is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Class C certification for the Cursor platform, and A-LIGN is performing the independent assessment. Certification has not yet been granted. Anysphere's FedRAMP 20x Class A application is under FedRAMP review. Origin, Cursor's Git hosting product, is not part of this offering and is not offered to FedRAMP customers; service capabilities that operate on Origin repositories are outside the assessed scope.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: The Cursor FedRAMP Trust Center, hosted on Paramify, publishes the FedRAMP 20x Class A and Class C compliance programs, provider-reported control implementation status, and controlled deliverables such as the SOC 2 Type II report for the Cursor platform.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: The compliance programs are viewable without an account. To review controlled deliverables, select Request Access on the FedRAMP Trust Center and identify your agency or organization. For control-level evidence, email fedramp@cursor.com from an official account to request read-only Paramify Assessment Viewer access. The Certification Package Overview is also available programmatically as JSON at https://cursor.com/fedramp/certification-package-overview.json through an unauthenticated HTTPS GET that returns application/json.

secureConfigurationGuidance.repositoryDescription: Public guidance for configuring identity, privacy, agent controls, network access, extensions, and monitoring for a secure Cursor deployment.

serviceProperties.securityCategoryNote: The adopting federal agency determines the applicable FIPS 199 security category for its intended use of each service. This package does not assert a provider-wide Low, Moderate, or High impact level.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Cursor IDE is a desktop code editor with AI-assisted code generation, review, navigation, and agent workflows built into the development environment.
supportingCapabilities: Rules, skills, hooks, plugins, and MCP integrations

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Cursor Agent CLI provides an interactive and headless coding agent in the terminal for writing, reviewing, and modifying code.
supportingCapabilities: Rules, skills, hooks, and MCP integrations

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Cursor Cloud Agents execute software development tasks in isolated cloud development environments and support parallel, long-running, scheduled, and event-driven workflows.
Cursor SDK provides programmatic access to the Cursor agent runtime for launching, steering, and composing agents in local and cloud environments.
Grok Bot provides AI teammates that work across connected tools using isolated cloud computers, carry tasks from start to finish, and continue working when users are away.
Bugbot reviews source code changes in supported source control systems, reports potential defects, and can propose fixes through Cursor agent workflows.
Security Agents review pull requests and scan codebases for security bugs, risky patterns, and vulnerabilities using Cursor-managed agents that run on Cloud Agents.
PR Routing & Approval routes pull requests to reviewers and approves low-risk changes when configured approval criteria are met.
Enterprise Administration provides organization and team management, identity and access controls, policy enforcement, usage and spend controls, audit and compliance logging, and administrative APIs.

documentationOverview.updateSource: Anysphere Security owner Ethan Troy's October 16 scheduling decisions set the first complete operating Ongoing Certification Report target to October 19, 2026 and adopt a report cycle every three calendar months on the 19th of October, January, April, and July, with subsequent targets January 19, April 19, and July 19, 2027. The owner also commits to October 22, 2026 as the first Quarterly Review target and next progress-update target. The report remains in progress after the prior October 11 and October 15 targets, and the review remains planned. The actual reporting period, report release, review timing, access, registration, and notice to necessary parties remain outstanding. The following is retained provenance for prior revision 2026-10-15: Anysphere Security owner Ethan Troy's October 15 planning decision revises the first operating Ongoing Certification Report target from October 11 to October 15 and retains October 15 as the proposed Quarterly Review target. The report remains in progress and the review remains planned; review timing and notice to necessary parties remain to be finalized. The other statements are unchanged from revision 2026-10-12, which marked the first Ongoing Certification Report as in progress. The other statements in that revision were unchanged from revision 2026-10-10, which added the FedRAMP 20x Class C progress section and matching JSON data, removed the published Class C progress update from materials in development, and aligned the next Ongoing Certification Report date with the approved schedule. The other statements in that revision were unchanged from revision 2026-10-07, which added that Anysphere's FedRAMP 20x Class A application is under FedRAMP review, checked against the status of that application with FedRAMP. The other statements in that revision were unchanged from revision 2026-09-28, which named the FedRAMP 20x Class C certification being pursued and its independent assessor (A-LIGN, FedRAMP assessor ID 138665; assessment in progress since 2026-09-15), described access to controlled FedRAMP Trust Center deliverables as a one-time approval, stated that Origin is not part of this offering, and stopped listing published materials as in development.

classCProgress.certificationStatus: FedRAMP 20x Class C certification has not yet been granted. Anysphere's FedRAMP 20x Class A application is under FedRAMP review.
classCProgress.goal: Obtain FedRAMP 20x Class C certification for the Cursor platform, publish an Ongoing Certification Report each quarter, and hold a Quarterly Review after each report.
classCProgress.updateCadence: Updated at least quarterly, and after each Quarterly Review. Progress is measured against the goal and milestones below.

milestones.title: Statement of work with the independent assessor
milestones.detail: A-LIGN, a FedRAMP recognized independent assessment service, performs the FedRAMP 20x Class C assessment of Cursor under a statement of work dated 2026-08-31.

milestones.title: Assessment kickoff
milestones.detail: Cursor and A-LIGN held the kickoff for the FedRAMP 20x Class C assessment.

milestones.title: Assessment activities began
milestones.detail: A-LIGN began assessing Cursor against the FedRAMP 20x Class C requirements.

milestones.title: Independent assessment determinations
milestones.detail: A-LIGN is recording its determinations on the FedRAMP 20x Class C requirements.

milestones.title: Submit remediation updates for assessor re-review
milestones.detail: Cursor plans to submit remediation updates to A-LIGN for re-review by 2026-10-16; other findings remain under remediation.

milestones.title: Class C assessment complete
milestones.detail: Cursor's target for A-LIGN to finalize the FedRAMP 20x Class C assessment.

milestones.title: Assessor's Overall Summary of Assessment added to the Certification Package Overview
milestones.detail: After the assessment is final, Cursor will include A-LIGN's Overall Summary of Assessment in its public Certification Package Overview without modification.

milestones.title: First Ongoing Certification Report
milestones.detail: Revised owner-adopted target for Cursor's first complete operating Ongoing Certification Report, previously targeted for 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-15. The October 15 target was not met; preparation remains in progress, and the available sample report is not a released operating report. The adopted report cycle is every three calendar months on the 19th of October, January, April, and July. Subsequent report targets are 2027-01-19, 2027-04-19, and 2027-07-19, replacing the prior 2026-12-08 subsequent-report target. These are scheduling commitments. The actual reporting period remains to be finalized; the operating report has not been issued or supplied.

milestones.title: First Quarterly Review
milestones.detail: Owner-adopted target for Cursor's first Quarterly Review, replacing the prior proposed 2026-10-15 target. October 22 is three business days after the planned October 19 report release. Validate the interval against the actual report release and applicable business-day calendar before scheduling. Meeting time, timezone, necessary-party registration, access, and notice remain to be finalized; no review has been held.
